**Example 5** Assume that Peet's Coffee is looking at two possible locations for a new shop. To help make a decision they look at the number of pedestrians that go by each of the two locations in one-hour segments. The results of the random sample are shown below:

>  [Location A Location B]{.underline}
>
> Mean number of pedestrians 421 347
>
> Sample standard deviation 122 85
>
> Number of hours sampled 35 50

Assume the two population variances are not known but equal. Complete the steps required to test the null and alternative hypothesis at the 1% level of significance that both sites have the same number of pedestrians and calculate the 95% confidence interval.

**[Step 1]{.underline}** H~0~: µ~1~ = µ~2~ , H~a~: µ~1~ ≠ µ~2~

**[Step 2]{.underline}** Using an α = .01, reject if the t test statistic is ≥2.576 =[FORMULA:ch10_q04_f08_image40.wmf] or if the p-Value is ≤ 0.01.

**[STEP 3]{.underline}** Since our t test statistic 3.30 \>[FORMULA:ch10_q04_f09_image41.emf]=2.576 and since our p-Value is .0014 \< α, we reject [FORMULA:ch10_q04_f10_image42.emf] . In addition, our hypothesized difference of 0 is not contained in the 95% confidence interval, but the mean difference of 74 is included in the confidence interval which confirms that we are correct in rejecting the null hypothesis. Thus, the difference in the means is statistically significant.

**[STEP 4]{.underline}** Given that our p-value is .0014, there is a overwhelming evidence or a highly statistically significant difference between the two sites. Thus, Peet's should use Location A for their new coffee shop.

**[Example 7]{.underline}** In a market research study conduct by Marilyn Merlot Winery on red wine preference, the following results were found. Of a sample of 500 men, 210 preferred red wine and of a sample of 500 women, 120 preferred red wine. Perform an hypothesis test to determine if the proportion of men preferring red wine is 25% higher than for women.

**[Step 1]{.underline}** H~0~: π~m~ -- π~w~ = 0, H~a~: π~m~ -- π~w~ \> .25

**[Step 2]{.underline}** Using an α = .05, reject H0 if the z test statistic is ≥ 1.645 or if the p-Value is ≤ 0.05.

**[Step 3]{.underline}** Select Hypothesis Tests, Compare Two Proportions, enter the data given the above problem, and click OK. Your dialogue box should look like the one shown below.

**[STEP 3]{.underline}** Since our z test statistic 6.05 \>[FORMULA:ch10_q04_f14_image44.emf] =1.645 and since our p-Value is 7.12E-10 \< α = .05, we reject H0. In addition, our hypothesized difference of 0 is not contained in the 95% confidence interval, but the sample mean difference 0.18 is contained within the 95% confidence interval which confirms that we are correct in rejecting the null hypothesis.

**[STEP 4]{.underline}** Given that we are rejecting H0, there is a statistically significant difference between the proportion of men who prefer red wine compared to women. There is overwhelming evidence that the proportion of men who prefer red wine is greater than 25% compared to the proportion of women.

A random sample of 8 pairs of identical 12-year-old twins took part in a study to see if vitamins helped their attention spans. For each pair, twin A was given a placebo, and twin B received a special vitamin supplement. A psychologist then determined the length of time (in minute) each remained with a puzzle. The results were

  -------- ------- ------- ------- ------- ------- ------- ------- -------
  Twin A     34      18      39      31      28      26      28      22

  Twin B     29      42      33      40      38      40      27      15
  -------- ------- ------- ------- ------- ------- ------- ------- -------

(a).Use a paired t procedure to test the hypothesis at the 0.05 level that the vitamin supplement gives recipients a longer attention span.

(b).Construct 95% confidence interval for the difference in the population means of the attention spans of twins given the placebo and the vitamin supplement.

questions.content:
Of a random sample of 148 accounting majors, 75 rated a sense of humor as a very important trait to their career performance. This same view was held by 81 of an independent random of 178 finance majors.

a\. Test, at the 5% level, the null hypothesis that at least one-half of all finance majors rate a sense of humor as very important.

b\. Test, at the 5% level against a two-sided alternative, the null hypothesis that the population proportions of accounting and finance majors who rate a sense of humor as very important are the same.

questions.content:
The production department of NDB Electronics wants to explore the relationship between the number of employees who assemble a subassembly and the number produced. As an experiment, two employees were assigned to assemble the subassemblies. They produced 15 during a one-hour period. Then four employees assembled them. They produced 25 during a one-hour period. The complete set of paired observations follows.

+:-----------------:+:---------------------------:+
| Number of         | One-Hour Production (units) |
|                   |                             |
| Assemblers        |                             |
+-------------------+-----------------------------+
| 2                 | 15                          |
+-------------------+-----------------------------+
| 4                 | 25                          |
+-------------------+-----------------------------+
| 1                 | 10                          |
+-------------------+-----------------------------+
| 5                 | 40                          |
+-------------------+-----------------------------+
| 3                 | 30                          |
+-------------------+-----------------------------+

The dependent variable is production; that is, it is assumed that the level of production depends upon the number of employee.

a.  Based on scatter diagram, does there appear to be any linear relationship between the number of assemblers and production? Explain.

b.  Determine the regression equation.

c.  Compute the coefficient of correlation.

d.  Predict the production of 6 employee.
